title: Experiment-driven launch checklist and pathways
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, experiment-first playbook for shipping a new product surface or major feature in small, observable stages. Focus is on quick probes, clear KPI fingerprints, and defined rollback/escape ladders rather than a single big-bang go/no-go.

Scope and when to use this doc:
- Use for any phased launch where traffic will be incrementally exposed (hosted API endpoints, feature flags, or dedicated customer pilots).
- Best for teams that want to iterate on safety, cost, latency, and quality signals across the first 30 days.
- Not intended to replace the canonical launch runbook for full enterprise migrations; this is a complementary, metric-first operational guide.

Core principles (experiment-driven):
1) Probe small, learn fast: prefer many short-duration probes (1–3 days) at low volume to longer blind ramps.
2) Signal-led decisions: each probe must have 3 primary signals (latency, error rate, output-quality) + 1 economic signal (cost/unit or tokens per request).
3) Ownership and timebox: every probe has a single owner and a clear stop time.
4) Contingency-first: predefine fallback variants and throttles; if an unknown failure appears, automate a graceful degradation path.

Hypotheses (example format)
- H1: New prompt template reduces median latency by 8% for 95th-percentile inputs without impacting quality (human eval pass rate >= 95%).
- H2: KV prefix caching reduces per-token cost by >= 15% for repeat-user traffic.
- H3: Model A quantized variant maintains NPS for sample customers within +-2 points of baseline.

Launch signals and KPI fingerprints (per-probe):
- Traffic slice: probe name + % of production traffic + cohort (internal beta / canary customers / random 1%).
- Latency: median and p95 tail (ms), SLO target and tolerance window (e.g., p95 < 350ms, tolerance 20ms).
- Errors: request error rate (5xx/4xx), categories (timeout, kernel OOM, model failure).
- Quality: automatic heuristics (embedding similarity delta, rerank accuracy) plus a small human-eval sample size and pass threshold.
- Cost: tokens/request and cost per 1k requests vs baseline.
- User experience: retention delta at 24–72h for cohorts (if applicable).

Signal thresholds (example):
- Green: latency and error within 5% of baseline + quality pass rate >= 95% + cost delta <= +5%
- Yellow: one signal outside green but within defined soft threshold (e.g., latency +10%, quality 90–94%) — hold and investigate for 24–48 hours
- Red: any critical signal breach (errors > 2x baseline or quality < 85% or cost delta > +30%) — immediate rollback or traffic cut to 0.

Data sources and dashboards:
- Lightweight dashboard: probe tiles with real-time p95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k requests, and a sketch of quality metric.
- Sources: Redwood Console route dashboards, Prometheus SLOs, Segment/Amplitude cohort tags, Human-eval spreadsheet.
- Quick access links: add the probe dashboard URL in the probe owner card before traffic change.

Owners and roles (example):
- Probe lead (owner): responsible for probe plan, executing traffic changes, and first 2h investigation.
- On-call SRE: responsible for infra escalations and kernel-level mitigations.
- Model owner (Applied ML): quality triage, rollback to model variants.
- Product ops: coordinates stakeholders, logs decisions, and files post-probe notes.

Pre-launch checklist (must be completed before any probe):
- Small checklist items (yes/no):
  - Route/config prepared with feature-flag or traffic-split ID.
  - Canary model variant registered and artifacts pinned.
  - Observability: dashboard tile created, Alert policies configured for red thresholds.
  - Smoke tests (unit and integration) pass in staging.
  - Latency budget documented for the probe and SRE aware.
  - Human-eval queue seeded with 30 examples for immediate quality checks.
  - Communication plan: Slack channel + escalation pager + email list.

Traffic phasing plan (template):
- Phase 0: internal-only probe (0.05% traffic or internal dev accounts) — 24–48h
- Phase 1: micro canary (0.5% traffic) — 48–72h, hold for stability signals
- Phase 2: targeted cohort (5% traffic, select segments) — 3–7 days, watch retention and cost
- Phase 3: gradual ramp (5% -> 25% over days) — hold windows for manual sign-off
- Phase 4: scale to full GA if all probes green and post-mortems complete

Contingency ladder and automated actions:
- Soft throttle: reduce new sessions by 50% if yellow thresholds persist > 24h (manual with one-click revert).
- Auto-cut: route back to baseline (0% for new model) if red threshold breached; trigger incident template and collect artifacts.
- Model fallback: config maps to fallback to smaller/older model variants with lower cost but proven stability.

Escalation template (first 60 minutes):
1) Probe owner notifies SRE and model owner; snapshot of last 15 minutes metrics posted to Slack.
2) Triage call if not resolved within 10 minutes; assign action items and owner for each task.
3) If severity high (traffic impact, customer-visible regressions), open incident in PagerDuty and use incident runbook.

Post-probe debrief (within 48 hours of probe finish):
- Short debrief notes (owner): what we observed, which signals trended, mitigations executed, A/B quality check outcome, and whether hypotheses held.
- Decision: promote to next phase, iterate and repeat probe, or revert and investigate root cause.
- Action items: assign owners, due dates, and link to tickets.

Templates and quick copy snippets (to paste into Slack / ticket):
- Probe kickoff (copy):
  Probe: [name]
  Owner: [name]
  Traffic slice: [x%] cohort: [description]
  Duration: [hours/days]
  Primary signals: latency p95 < [X]ms, errors < [Y%], quality pass >= [Z%]
  Dashboard: [link]
  Rollback plan: [one-line]

- Probe close summary (copy):
  Probe: [name] — status: [green/yellow/red]
  Key observations: [bullets]
  Decision: [promote/repeat/revert]
  Actions: [ticket links]

Operational notes and gotchas (lessons learned bucket):
- Small traffic slices can hide cold start issues; run a synthetic burst to reveal cold-KV and cache warmup problems.
- Cost signals are lagging — include sampling to compute per-request token entropy under low traffic.
- Human-eval sampling size matters: 30 samples is minimal for a quick sanity check; use 100+ for statistical confidence if moving beyond canary.
- Don’t conflate small improvements in latency with quality; prefer to gate on concrete quality metrics for user-facing features.

Weekly cadence and sign-off gates (recommended):
- Weekly probe review: list of active probes, owners, and readiness to escalate to next phase.
- Product ops gate: ensures docs updated, tickets created for each action, and final business sign-off before larger ramps.

Appendix: quick checklist for experiment readiness (copyable)
- [ ] Dashboard tile + alert configured
- [ ] Probe owner and SRE on-call assigned
- [ ] Human-eval queue seeded
- [ ] Rollback variant tested in staging
- [ ] Communication channels ready

Notes and references:
- This is a living doc: add probe retros and keep the lessons-learned section updated.
- If a probe exposes a platform reliability bug, follow the SRE incident retro flow and mark the probe as paused until fix validated.
